stages.masters: Direct-entry PhD track (no standalone terminal master's); attend IAS Women and Mathematics (WAM).
stages.phd: Arguably the world's most competitive pure mathematics PhD in Fine Hall.
stages.postdoc: IAS School of Mathematics Memberships and Princeton Instructor / Veblen Research Instructorships.
stages.assoc_prof: Joint Fine Hall – IAS research collaborations and Annals of Mathematics editorial work.
stages.prof: Permanent Faculty chairs at Princeton University and the Institute for Advanced Study.

rabbitLinks.reason: Adjacent to Jadwin Hall Physics and the Institute for Advanced Study where Einstein and Witten worked.
Alan Turing earned his PhD in Princeton's Fine Hall under Alonzo Church in 1938 right after inventing the Turing machine.
Andrew Wiles worked in secret for 7 years in Princeton before unveiling his proof of Fermat's Last Theorem at Cambridge's Newton Institute.

projects.name: Annals of Mathematics & IAS Special Year Programs

hubs.name: Cambridge Centre for Mathematical Sciences (DAMTP & DPMMS)
hubs.summary: Unites Pure Mathematics (DPMMS) and Applied Mathematics & Theoretical Physics (DAMTP)—historic home of Newton's Lucasian Chair, G.H. Hardy, Ramanujan, Paul Dirac, Alan Turing, and Stephen Hawking.
hubs.nobel: Fields Medalists include Alan Baker, Richard Borcherds, Timothy Gowers, and Caucher Birkar; Nobel laureate Paul Dirac held the Lucasian Chair.

stages.highschool: Solve NRICH and STEP (Sixth Term Examination Paper) problems created by Cambridge mathematicians.
stages.undergrad: Cambridge Mathematical Tripos (Parts IA, IB, II) — legendary problem-sheet training.
stages.masters: Part III of the Mathematical Tripos (MASt) — the world's most celebrated 1-year graduate math course.
stages.phd: PhD in Pure Math, Cosmology, Fluid Dynamics, Quantum Information, and Mathematical Genomics.
stages.postdoc: Cambridge College Research Fellowships (Trinity, King's, St John's) and Royal Society Fellowships.
stages.assoc_prof: University Associate Professorships bridging pure math with theoretical physics.
stages.prof: Historic chairs including the Lucasian, Rouse Ball, and Sadleirian Professorships.

rabbitLinks.reason: Home to Stephen Hawking's cosmology group and David Tong's famous open QFT/physics lecture notes.
Shares the Wilberforce Road campus with the Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences.
Historic Cambridge-India bond forged when Srinivasa Ramanujan arrived at Trinity College to collaborate with G.H. Hardy.

projects.name: Part III Mathematical Tripos & Millennium Mathematics Project

hubs.name: ETH Zurich Department of Mathematics (D-MATH)
hubs.summary: Housed in ETH's iconic main building overlooking Zurich—where Hermann Weyl, Heinz Hopf, George Pólya, and Marcel Grossmann (who taught Einstein Riemannian geometry) built a powerhouse in analysis, probability, and mathematical physics.
hubs.nobel: Home to Fields Medalists Alessio Figalli (2018, optimal transport) and Wendelin Werner (2006), plus the ETH Institute for Theoretical Studies (ETH-ITS).

stages.highschool: Read George Pólya's classic 'How to Solve It'—written by a longtime ETH Zurich math professor.
stages.undergrad: ETH Zurich BSc in Mathematics (open admission for Swiss Matura; rigorous analysis foundation).
stages.masters: ETH MSc in Mathematics or Applied Mathematics (taught in English).
stages.phd: Fully salaried Swiss PhD positions across FIM (Forschungsinstitut für Mathematik) and SAM.
stages.postdoc: ETH-ITS Fellows and FIM Postdoctoral Fellowships uniting pure math and theoretical physics.
stages.assoc_prof: Tenure-track professorships in optimal transport, stochastics, numerical PDEs, and data science.
stages.prof: Visiting Professorships via FIM hosting hundreds of global mathematicians each year.

rabbitLinks.reason: ETH mathematician Marcel Grossmann introduced his former classmate Albert Einstein to Riemannian tensors for General Relativity.
D-MATH's Seminar for Applied Mathematics (SAM) underpins neural PDE solvers and AI theory.

projects.name: Forschungsinstitut für Mathematik (FIM) & ETH-ITS

hubs.name: African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS South Africa)
hubs.summary: Africa's first pan-African network of centers of excellence in mathematical sciences—founded by cosmologist Neil Turok in Muizenberg and now spanning South Africa, Senegal, Ghana, Cameroon, and Rwanda.
hubs.nobel: Trained 3,000+ African master's graduates from 45+ countries; home to the African Master's in Machine Intelligence (AMMI) backed by Google & Meta.

stages.highschool: Engage with AIMSSEC teacher enrichment programs strengthening school mathematics across Africa.
stages.undergrad: Prepare for the fully funded AIMS Structured Master's Programme in Mathematical Sciences.
stages.masters: 1-year intensive residential MSc (100% scholarships) taught by visiting professors from around the world.
stages.phd: AIMS-South Africa & Quantum Leap Africa PhD tracks in data science, cosmology, and climate math.
stages.postdoc: AIMS Research Centre postdoctoral fellowships in epidemiology, climate modeling, and AI.
stages.assoc_prof: Volunteer as a 3-week visiting lecturer teaching specialized modules to Africa's top math students.
stages.prof: Hold AIMS Research Chairs (including German Research Chairs supported by Humboldt Foundation).

rabbitLinks.reason: AIMS graduates analyze petabytes of radio astronomy data from South Africa's MeerKAT and Square Kilometre Array.
Founded by cosmologist Neil Turok before he directed Perimeter Institute, creating a lasting Canada-Africa math bridge.
AIMS mathematical epidemiologists collaborate with South African genomic surveillance teams on infectious disease modeling.

projects.name: AI for Science Master's (with Google DeepMind) & Next Einstein Forum

hubs.name: University of Oxford Mathematical Institute
hubs.summary: Housed in the landmark Andrew Wiles Building, one of the world's largest and strongest mathematics departments spanning analytic number theory, algebraic geometry, topology, mathematical logic, and mathematical physics.
hubs.nobel: Home to Abel laureate Andrew Wiles (Fermat's Last Theorem), 2020 Physics Nobel laureate Roger Penrose, and 2022 Fields Medalist James Maynard.

projects.name: Number Theory, Geometry & Langlands Research Groups

hubs.name: ICMAT (Instituto de Ciencias Matemáticas)
hubs.summary: Spain's flagship Severo Ochoa mathematical research institute (jointly operated by CSIC, UAM, UC3M, and UCM) excelling in algebraic geometry, moduli spaces, differential geometry, number theory, and fluid PDEs.
hubs.nobel: Consistently awarded Spain's Severo Ochoa Centre of Excellence distinction and numerous European Research Council (ERC) grants.

projects.name: ICMAT Thematic Laboratories in Geometry & Number Theory

hubs.name: Scuola Normale Superiore – Centro De Giorgi
hubs.summary: Italy's elite graduate university and Centro di Ricerca Matematica Ennio De Giorgi in Pisa—legendary incubator of algebraic geometry, Diophantine number theory, calculus of variations, and optimal transport.
hubs.nobel: Nurtured Fields Medalists Enrico Bombieri (1974) and Alessio Figalli (2018), alongside Wolf Prize laureate Ennio De Giorgi.

projects.name: Centro De Giorgi Intensive Research Periods

hubs.name: The Institute of Mathematical Sciences (IMSc)
hubs.summary: National fundamental research institute in Chennai founded by Alladi Ramakrishnan—famous for algebraic geometry, analytic number theory, representation theory, theoretical computer science, and quantum gravity.
hubs.nobel: Inspired by Niels Bohr and the IAS Princeton model; home to multiple Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar and Infosys Prize laureates in mathematics.

projects.name: Number Theory, Algebraic Geometry & Representation Theory

hubs.name: CIRM (Centre International de Rencontres Mathématiques)
hubs.summary: France's residential mathematical retreat nestled in the Calanques National Park of Marseille, run by CNRS and the Société Mathématique de France to host 90+ week-long international workshops and Jean-Morlet Chairs annually.
hubs.nobel: Welcomes ~5,000 visiting mathematicians each year across PDEs, dynamical systems, algebraic geometry, and mathematical physics.

projects.name: Jean-Morlet Chair Semesters & Audiovisual Math Library

hubs.name: Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics (IPAM), UCLA
hubs.summary: NSF-funded national mathematics institute at UCLA (home to Fields Medalist Terence Tao), running long programs uniting harmonic analysis, nonlinear PDEs, mathematical imaging, materials modeling, and AI theory.
hubs.nobel: Directly partnered with UCLA Mathematics (Terence Tao, Stanley Osher, Andrea Bertozzi) and renowned for its RIPS undergraduate research program.

projects.name: IPAM Long Programs & RIPS Summer Research

hubs.name: Institut Henri Poincaré (IHP)
hubs.summary: Historic 'Maison des Mathématiques' in Paris's Latin Quarter hosting international thematic trimesters in PDEs, geometry, probability, and theoretical physics—alongside the Maison Poincaré mathematics museum.
hubs.nobel: Directed by Émile Borel and later 2010 Fields Medalist Cédric Villani; historic home of the Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincaré.

projects.name: IHP Thematic Trimesters & Maison Poincaré Museum

hubs.name: Stanford Department of Statistics & ICME
hubs.summary: World-leading hub for modern mathematical statistics, statistical learning, compressed sensing, and computational engineering—uniting Stanford Statistics with the Institute for Computational & Mathematical Engineering (ICME).
hubs.nobel: Home to International Prize in Statistics laureate Bradley Efron (bootstrap), David Donoho, Emmanuel Candès, Trevor Hastie, and Rob Tibshirani.

projects.name: Statistical Learning, Conformal Prediction & Compressed Sensing

hubs.name: MIT Department of Mathematics (Applied Mathematics)
hubs.summary: Powerhouse of applied mathematics, numerical linear algebra, scientific computing (birthplace of the Julia language), physical applied math, combinatorics, and quantum algorithms inside MIT's Building 2.
hubs.nobel: Home to Peter Shor (Shor's quantum factoring algorithm), Gilbert Strang (linear algebra educator), and Abel Prize laureate Isadore Singer's legacy.

projects.name: Julia Scientific Computing & Physical Applied Math Lab

hubs.name: Oxford Centre for Industrial and Applied Mathematics (OCIAM)
hubs.summary: World-leading applied mathematics research group inside Oxford's Andrew Wiles Building, pioneering mathematical modeling for batteries, continuum mechanics, fluid flows, and industrial Study Groups.
hubs.nobel: Invented the globally replicated European Study Groups with Industry (ESGI) model connecting rigorous asymptotic PDEs with real-world engineering.

projects.name: Mathematical Modelling of Energy Storage & Continuum Mechanics

hubs.name: ETH Zurich Seminar for Statistics (SfS)
hubs.summary: Continental Europe's foremost center for mathematical statistics and causal inference within ETH D-MATH, advancing high-dimensional statistics, robust estimation, distributional robustness, and statistical learning theory.
hubs.nobel: Led by Peter Bühlmann, Nicolai Meinshausen, and Sara van de Geer—pioneers of high-dimensional Lasso theory and invariance-based causal inference.

projects.name: Causal Inference & High-Dimensional Statistical Learning

hubs.name: Columbia University Department of Statistics
hubs.summary: Historic statistics powerhouse founded by Abraham Wald and Harold Hotelling, today driving Bayesian computation (Stan probabilistic programming), variational inference, causal inference, and probabilistic machine learning.
hubs.nobel: Home to Abraham Wald's sequential analysis legacy alongside Andrew Gelman (Stan) and David Blei (Latent Dirichlet Allocation & variational inference).

projects.name: Stan Probabilistic Programming & Bayesian Workflow

hubs.name: University of Chicago Department of Statistics
hubs.summary: Renowned theoretical and applied statistics department bridging deep mathematical probability, statistical genetics, tensor algebra, optimal transport, and foundations of machine learning.
hubs.nobel: Shaped by Leonard Savage, Patrick Billingsley, and Stephen Stigler; closely linked with UChicago's Committee on Computational and Applied Mathematics.

projects.name: Mathematical Statistics, Genetics & Data Science Foundations

hubs.name: Indian Statistical Institute (ISI)
hubs.summary: Iconic national institution of importance founded by Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis—birthplace of the Mahalanobis distance, Cramér-Rao inequality, and India's premier school of probability, statistics, and theoretical CS.
hubs.nobel: Home to 2023 International Prize in Statistics laureate C.R. Rao and Abel Prize laureate S.R.S. Varadhan (PhD 1963).

projects.name: Sankhya Journal & Theoretical Statistics and Probability Unit

hubs.name: KAUST CEMSE Applied Mathematics & Computational Science
hubs.summary: Middle East's flagship applied mathematics and statistics division on the Red Sea coast, advancing exascale numerical PDEs, federated and stochastic optimization, spatio-temporal climate statistics, and Shaheen III supercomputing.
hubs.nobel: Home to Extreme Computing Research Center and world-leading groups in federated optimization and extreme-value environmental statistics.

projects.name: Extreme Computing & Stochastic Optimization Programs

hubs.name: Caltech Computing and Mathematical Sciences (CMS)
hubs.summary: Interdisciplinary Caltech department uniting applied mathematics, randomized numerical linear algebra, Bayesian inverse problems, neural operators for PDEs, and algorithmic economics.
hubs.nobel: Pioneered Fourier Neural Operators (FNO) for scientific PDEs and matrix concentration inequalities underpinning randomized algorithms.

projects.name: Neural Operators, Inverse Problems & Randomized Linear Algebra

hubs.name: KTH & Stockholm University Mathematical Statistics
hubs.summary: Continues Harald Cramér's historic Stockholm school of probability and mathematical statistics—advancing stochastic processes, spatial statistics, actuarial risk theory, epidemic modeling, and mathematical machine learning.
hubs.nobel: Harald Cramér established foundational large-deviations theory and the Cramér-Rao lower bound in Stockholm's probability tradition.

projects.name: Stochastic Processes, Epidemic Modeling & Risk Theory

hubs.name: Imperial College London Department of Mathematics
hubs.summary: Premier London mathematics department spanning stochastic PDEs, mathematical finance, statistical machine learning, fluid dynamics, and Lean formalization of modern number theory.
hubs.nobel: Home to Fields Medalists Martin Hairer (2014, regularity structures for SPDEs) and Simon Donaldson (1986), plus Lean evangelist Kevin Buzzard.

projects.name: Stochastic Analysis, Mathematical Finance & Xena Lean Project

hubs.name: Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics
hubs.summary: World capital of extremal combinatorics, graph theory, discrete geometry, and probabilistic methods—founded by Alfréd Rényi and shaped by Paul Erdős's legendary problem-solving legacy.
hubs.nobel: Home to Abel Prize laureates Endre Szemerédi (2012, arithmetic progressions) and László Lovász (2021, graph limits & algorithms).

projects.name: Erdős Center & Graph Limits / Combinatorics Programs

hubs.name: Stefan Banach International Mathematical Center (IMPAN)
hubs.summary: Central European international conference and research institute of the Polish Academy of Sciences continuing the historic Polish School of topology, set theory, logic, and Banach-space functional analysis.
hubs.nobel: Carries forward the foundational legacy of Stefan Banach, Alfred Tarski, Kazimierz Kuratowski, and the Lwów-Warsaw mathematical schools.

projects.name: Banach Center Thematic Semesters & Topology Publications

hubs.name: Kurt Gödel Research Center for Mathematical Logic (KGRC)
hubs.summary: University of Vienna research institute honoring Kurt Gödel's incompleteness breakthroughs, dedicated to set theory, large cardinals, forcing, descriptive set theory, and the foundations of mathematics.
hubs.nobel: Located in the city where Kurt Gödel proved his 1931 Incompleteness Theorems; a premier global node for set-theoretic logic.

projects.name: Set Theory, Large Cardinals & Forcing Research

hubs.name: CMU Hoskinson Center for Formal Mathematics
hubs.summary: Carnegie Mellon research center led by Jeremy Avigad advancing machine-checked formal mathematics in Lean 4, homotopy type theory, automated reasoning, and open educational libraries for formal proof.
hubs.nobel: Co-authored 'Mathematics in Lean' and bridges philosophical logic, type theory, and AI-assisted theorem proving.

projects.name: Formal Mathematics in Lean 4 & Automated Reasoning

hubs.name: Lean Focused Research Organization (Lean FRO)
hubs.summary: Non-profit focused research organization led by Leonardo de Moura and Sebastian Ullrich engineering the Lean 4 interactive theorem prover and scaling the global Mathlib formalized mathematics library.
hubs.nobel: Lean 4 powers the Liquid Tensor Experiment, Fermat's Last Theorem formalization, and AI neuro-symbolic proof systems worldwide.

projects.name: Lean 4 Proof Assistant & Mathlib4 Library

hubs.name: University of Waterloo Dept. of Combinatorics & Optimization
hubs.summary: The world's only standalone university department dedicated exclusively to combinatorics and optimization—founded by Bletchley Park cryptanalyst and graph-theory pioneer W.T. Tutte—spanning graph theory, cryptography, and quantum information.
hubs.nobel: Founded by W.T. Tutte (Lorenz cipher breaker & matroid theory pioneer); tightly linked with IQC and Perimeter Institute.

projects.name: Graph Theory, Algebraic Combinatorics & Post-Quantum Crypto

hubs.name: Einstein Institute of Mathematics, Hebrew University
hubs.summary: Historic mathematics institute on Jerusalem's Givat Ram campus—globally celebrated for mathematical logic, model theory, ergodic theory, algebraic combinatorics, and game theory.
hubs.nobel: Home to Fields Medalist Elon Lindenstrauss (2010), Abel laureate Hillel Furstenberg (2020), Wolf laureate Saharon Shelah (logic), and Economics Nobel laureate Robert Aumann.

projects.name: Model Theory, Combinatorics & Ergodic Theory Groups

hubs.name: Technion Faculty of Mathematics
hubs.summary: Leading Israeli mathematics faculty in Haifa excelling in extremal and topological combinatorics, convex and discrete geometry, spectral graph theory, convex optimization, and mathematical physics.
hubs.nobel: Renowned for topological combinatorics, matrix theory, and continuous-discrete optimization feeding directly into Technion's CS and engineering hubs.

projects.name: Combinatorics, Discrete Geometry & Optimization

hubs.name: Centre de Recherches Mathématiques (CRM Montréal)
hubs.summary: Canada's oldest national mathematical sciences research institute, uniting 13 Quebec and Ontario universities across algebraic combinatorics (LaCIM), topology, mathematical physics, and mathematical AI.
hubs.nobel: Awards the prestigious CRM-Fields-PIMS Prize and anchors Montreal's mathematical bridge to Mila's deep learning ecosystem.

projects.name: CRM Thematic Semesters & LaCIM Combinatorics Lab

hubs.name: UC Berkeley Group in Logic and the Methodology of Science
hubs.summary: Interdisciplinary doctoral and research center founded by Alfred Tarski at UC Berkeley—the historic epicenter of model theory, set theory, recursion theory, and mathematical foundations.
hubs.nobel: Founded by Alfred Tarski and shaped by Julia Robinson, Robert Solovay, Hugh Woodin, and Thomas Scanlon.

projects.name: Model Theory, Set Theory & Computability Seminars

hubs.name: University of Bonn Discrete Mathematics & Logic Institute
hubs.summary: Home to the Arithmeum museum and Bonn's world-renowned Research Institute for Discrete Mathematics & Mathematical Logic—pioneering combinatorial VLSI chip layout optimization alongside Bonn's set-theory and logic groups.
hubs.nobel: BonnTools combinatorial algorithms developed by Bernhard Korte and Jens Vygen have routed billions of transistors on IBM microprocessor chips.

projects.name: BonnTools Combinatorial Optimization & Set Theory
